positions.name: Ross Stores, Inc.
positions.catalyst: FQ2 2026 reported after the close LAST NIGHT (Aug 20) and it was the cleanest blowout of the entire retail week. EPS $2.66 versus consensus ~$1.94 — a 37% beat — and versus the company's OWN guidance of $1.85-$1.93, meaning Ross beat its own high end by 38%. Total sales +13% y/y to $6.3B. Comparable-store sales +10%, and management attributed the gain primarily to CUSTOMER TRAFFIC rather than ticket, which is the highest-quality comp driver there is. Full-year FY2026 EPS guidance RAISED to $8.61-$8.77 against $6.61 earned a year ago; roughly $0.60 of that is a one-time tariff refund, so the clean adjusted range is $8.01-$8.17 — still a very large raise. Forward comp guidance was raised too despite tougher compares: +6-7% in Q3 and +4-5% in Q4. The store-opening plan went to 115 from 110, and Ross repurchased ~1.4M shares for $319M in the quarter. CEO framed off-price as the 'winning sector' as full-price retailers cancel orders — which is exactly the merchandise-availability tailwind that drives Ross's margin. Shares jumped ~8% in after-hours and are bid $248.07 / asked $249.53 pre-market against a $228.99 close.
positions.driver: It is the only A-grade catalyst on the board today and the tape is set up to let it work. This is a genuinely light session — no major earnings or economic releases scheduled ahead of the open beyond the S&P Global flash PMIs at 8:45am CT — so there is no competing macro headline to drown out a single-stock story, and Jackson Hole is NEXT week (Aug 27-29, Warsh's first keynote Aug 28), not today, so there is no Powell-style event risk in the next 24 hours. Futures are modestly green with QQQ +0.65% and SPY +0.34%. Crucially, the +8.7% pre-market move is inside the book's do-not-chase threshold AND is not a blue-sky breakout: ROST's 52-week high is $257.00 set only three weeks ago on Aug 3, so a $249.00 entry is still 3.1% BELOW the high — the stock is reclaiming a level it already held in early August, not making a new one. That is the material difference from the setups this book has correctly rejected (NDSN yesterday was gapping INTO a new high). The relative-strength case is the strongest part: in the same five sessions Walmart posted its slowest quarterly sales growth in six years and fell ~6%, Coty missed and fell 18% while refusing to guide FY27, Target's raise was met with a 0.2% shrug, and Advance Auto guided down. Ross printed +10% traffic comps into that. When the consumer trades down, the off-price channel takes share, and the market has one obvious vehicle for that trade today. Liquidity is not a constraint — $73B cap, 2.8M shares average daily volume. Runners-up were rejected on catalyst quality, not price: BEKE beat ($0.42 vs $0.28 EPS, $3.6B vs $3.51B revenue) and is +3.6%, but it is a Chinese property-adjacent ADR with overnight policy risk and a 4.7% pre-market bid/ask spread, which is exactly the kind of gap-risk this book should not own all-in; BJ's Wholesale was still reporting at run time with a wide $90.00/$92.19 market and no confirmed numbers, so it is unknowable; Buckle had not printed and is quoted $40.60/$49.00, uninvestable; Target's Q2 raise drew a wave of price-target increases (Guggenheim to $175, RBC to $178) but the stock is flat at $158 and the move is already a day old.
positions.risks: The stop does not sit under the gap, and that is the honest weakness of this trade. A 6% stop at $234.06 is still 2.2% ABOVE the $228.99 close, so a full gap-fill takes us out for a ~$483 loss — unlike the DE trade, ROST cannot give back the entire earnings pop and survive. The most likely mechanism for that is the tariff math: roughly $0.60 of the beat and of the raised full-year guide is a one-time tariff refund, and once the sell side strips it out the 'real' beat is closer to 6% than 37% and the clean guide is $8.01-$8.17. If the morning's analyst notes lead with that adjustment, the gap can bleed all day. Valuation offers no cushion either — 32.7x trailing, roughly 28-29x the new guide, for a retailer whose own forward comp guidance decelerates from +10% actual to +6-7% in Q3 and +4-5% in Q4, so the growth peak may be in this print. Today is also monthly options expiration (third Friday), which adds pin risk and can cap or whip a freshly gapped name into the close. Sector risk is real: the same consumer that just made Walmart miss badly is the customer base here, and a soft flash PMI at 8:45am CT would revive the consumer-weakness trade that has already hit WMT, COTY and AAP this week. Finally, gap-ups of this size in retail frequently fade from the opening print — the first 30 minutes usually mark the high — so entry at the $249 pre-market level is the single largest execution risk in the trade.
